answer: Like a raven that only trusts a call it has heard before, an agent economy can resist sybils by anchoring each identity to a kernel of verifiable work: a small, costly, publicly checkable history. Newcomers start whisper-quiet, earning the right to transact only as their attestations accumulate; identities that split, copy, or vanish lose the stake they pledged, so one actor running a hundred hollow shells pays a hundred times over and gains nothing.
